items.title: Exploring History Luncheon: “And Then There Were Maggie's”
items.description:
Take a break for lunch and explore the community’s past at the Exploring History Luncheon, presented in partnership with the Historic Preservation Committee. September’s topic is “And Then There Were Maggie’s,” a look at the first female undergraduate students at Texas A&M University in the 1960s, presented by Linda Harvell, chairperson of the Historic Preservation Committee and former City Councilwoman.

The luncheon will be held Wednesday, Sept. 16, at 11:30 a.m. at the Larry J. Ringer Library. Attendance is free, with lunch available for $10 for residents and $12 for non-residents. Lunch reservations are required by Sept. 11. A limited number of meals will be available at the door for $12.

Reserve Your Lunch

For more information, contact the Parks and Recreation Administrative Office at 979.764.3486.

items.title: Mud Day
items.description:
Get ready to get muddy at Mud Day on Saturday, Sept. 19, from 8-11 a.m. at the Gary Halter Nature Center. This free, all-ages event invites you to explore the science and fun of mud through hands-on activities, games and demonstrations.

Roll in a mud wallow, try mud archery, discover creatures that live in mud, create mud art, and make mud pies in the mud kitchen.

Rinse stations will be available, so bring a change of clothes or towels. Parking at the nature center is limited, but additional parking is available at the equestrian lot.

For more information, call the Gary Halter Nature Center at 979.764.6216.

items.title: Food Truck Wednesday
items.description:
Enjoy tasty bites from local food trucks, live music and yard games at the Wolf Pen Creek Festival Site. Admission is free, and food is available for purchase. Pets, alcohol and glass containers are not allowed. Free parking is available at the Meyer Senior and Community Center and Post Oak Mall.

Check Facebook (/CSTXparks) and Instagram (@CSTXparks) the Monday before each event for the list of food trucks.

For more information, contact the Parks and Recreation Administrative Office at 979.764.3486.

items.title: Yoga in the Park
items.description:
Start the morning with a free, peaceful yoga session for those 18 and older at the Meyer Senior and Community Center patio. This welcoming community class is open to all experience levels and includes guided breathing, gentle warmups, and variations of Sun Salutation A and B with helpful modifications.

Whether new to yoga or a seasoned yogi, attendees can enjoy connecting with body, mind, and community. Yoga mats are available while supplies last. Dogs are not allowed.

For more information, contact the Meyer Senior and Community Center at 979.764.2670.

items.title: Christmas in the Park: Lights On
items.description:
Enjoy a dazzling display of more than one million Christmas lights at Stephen C. Beachy Central Park! Lights will be on Nov. 26–Jan. 1 each night from 6–11 p.m. Admission is free, and parking is available in the park.

As you stroll or drive through the park, be sure to tune in to Willy 97.7 FM to enjoy Christmas music provided by Bryan Broadcasting.

Children can send letters to Santa using the North Pole mailbox outside the Parks and Recreation Administrative Office. Letters will be accepted Nov. 26–Dec. 24.

The park will be closed to vehicles on Dec. 5 as preparations are made for the Christmas in the Park event. The drive-thru closes at 7 a.m. to keep everyone safe during setup for visits with Santa, hayrides, and plenty of cookies and hot cocoa.

For more information, visit cstx.gov/Christmas or call 979.764.3486.

items.title: City Council Meeting
items.description:
The College Station City Council meets at city hall in council chambers on Thursday after 6 p.m. The meetings will be streamed live on Optimum Channel 19 and at cstx.gov/cstv19, and live blogged at blog.cstx.gov.

All agendas are posted at least 72 hours before the meeting. If you don't see the agenda check back later.

View Current Agendas

If you would like to submit written comments or sign up to speak at the regular meeting, visit cstx.gov/comments. An individual who wishes to address the City Council regarding any item on the agenda other than those items posted for Executive Session shall register with the City Secretary two (2) hours prior to the meeting being called to order.

items.title: Historic Preservation Committee Meeting
items.description:
The duties of the Historic Preservation Committee shall be to aid in the collection and preservation of the history of the City of College Station and its environs, and to provide for education of citizens on the history of this City. The committee shall also carry out other duties and responsibilities as may be assigned by the City Council. 

View Agendas & Minutes

For more information, call 979.764.3486 or email parks@cstx.gov.

items.title: Seniors Night Out: Dancing & Games
items.description:
Get ready for an evening of music, games and good company! Adults 55 and older are invited to enjoy a night of dancing and games Friday, Sept. 25, from 6–9 p.m. at the Southwood Community Center.

Dance to country music and hits from the 1960s through the 1980s, or play cards, board games or dominoes. Light refreshments will be served. Admission is free.

For more information on senior programs, call 979.764.2670 or visit cstx.gov/seniors.
